          "text": "# Beta Ara: A Southern Beacon in the Altar\n\n*Bright enough for the unaided eye, this distant giant marks a rewarding stop in the southern sky.*\n\nBeta Ara sits in Ara, the Altar, at a far-southern declination of about 55.5 degrees below the celestial equator. In a dark sky it is an easy naked-eye star: the SIMBAD astronomical database lists its visual magnitude as 2.85. Its catalogue position is right ascension 17 hours 25 minutes and declination \u221255 degrees 31 minutes. Those coordinates put it well south of the familiar northern constellations\u2014and make it a natural target for observers in the Southern Hemisphere. ([SIMBAD: HIP 85258 / Beta Ara](https://simbad.cds.unistra.fr/simbad/sim-id?Ident=HIP%2085258))\n\nAra is sometimes imagined as a small ceremonial altar, but in the sky it is a pattern of stars rather than a sharply drawn object. Beta Ara is one of its bright markers: a point of light to seek out after identifying the surrounding shape on a star chart. Its brightness does not mean it is close. SIMBAD reports a parallax of 4.5601 milliarcseconds.
